content.text: I have enough breadth now to compile the products facet survey.

items.name: Claude (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku / Fable)
items.detail: Anthropic's model family; as of mid-2026 the lineup is Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and a new top tier, Fable 5 (released July 2026), with Sonnet/Opus/Fable at 1M-token context.

items.name: Claude Code
items.detail: Anthropic's terminal-native autonomous coding agent, widely cited in coding-agent comparisons for context size and SWE-bench performance.

items.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.6 (ChatGPT)
items.detail: OpenAI's flagship reasoning model family, now shipped as the GPT-5.6 family with named variants Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced) and Luna (cost-efficient), underpinning ChatGPT.

items.name: ChatGPT
items.detail: OpenAI's consumer/enterprise assistant product, now a broader platform with Images, Voice, Tasks, Memory and Custom GPTs layered on the GPT-5.x models.

items.name: OpenAI Codex
items.detail: OpenAI's agentic coding product/model line, also offered through partners such as AWS Bedrock; competes directly with Claude Code and Cursor.

items.name: Sora
items.detail: OpenAI's text/image-to-video and audio generation model; Sora 2 improved realism, physics simulation, audio and controllability.

items.name: Stargate
items.detail: OpenAI-led ~$500B, multi-year US (and international) data-center buildout with SoftBank, Oracle and MGX, with confirmed sites including Abilene TX and Saline Township MI; press covers it as the industry's flagship compute-infrastructure project.

items.name: Gemini 3
items.detail: Google DeepMind's current frontier model family (Pro, DeepThink, Flash variants), released from November 2025 with subsequent point releases (3.5/3.6 Flash, Flash-Lite, Flash Cyber) through 2026.

items.name: Google Antigravity
items.detail: Google's AI-assisted software development platform built on Gemini 3, positioned against Cursor/Claude Code/Copilot in agentic coding.

items.name: Gemma
items.detail: Google DeepMind's open-weight model family, the openly licensed counterpart to closed Gemini models.

items.name: Veo
items.detail: Google DeepMind's text/image-to-video generation model (Veo 3.1 cited in 2026 for multi-input creative control), a direct competitor to Sora, Runway and Kling.

items.name: Nvidia Blackwell / Blackwell Ultra
items.detail: Nvidia's prior-generation GPU architecture (GB200/GB300 systems) still in wide deployment through 2026 as the installed base ahead of Rubin.

items.name: Nvidia Rubin
items.detail: Nvidia's next-generation GPU platform (Rubin GPU + Vera CPU + NVLink 6 etc.), TSMC 3nm, shipping H2 2026 via AWS/Google Cloud/Microsoft/OCI; the chip generation the market watches most closely.

items.name: Nvidia CUDA
items.detail: Nvidia's parallel-computing software platform/API, the foundational lock-in layer underlying essentially all Nvidia AI hardware coverage.

items.name: Nvidia NIM
items.detail: Nvidia's packaged inference microservices for deploying models (including its Cosmos Reason line) on Blackwell/Rubin rack-scale systems.

items.name: Nvidia DGX / DGX Cloud
items.detail: Nvidia's integrated AI system/appliance line and its cloud-hosted equivalent, paired with Omniverse for industrial and physical-AI workloads.

items.name: Nvidia Omniverse
items.detail: Nvidia's simulation/digital-twin platform for industrial and physical AI, made free for production use in 2026 and integrated with major CAD/manufacturing vendors.

items.name: Mistral Large 3
items.detail: Mistral AI's flagship 675B-parameter model, released December 2025, Apache 2.0 licensed like most of Mistral's line.

items.name: Mistral Medium / Small / Ministral
items.detail: Mistral's mid-size and small/edge model tiers (Medium 3.5, Small 4, Ministral 3 at 14B/8B/3B), the bulk of its self-hostable open-weight catalog.

items.name: Mistral Forge
items.detail: Mistral's enterprise platform for training fully custom models on proprietary data, distinct from simple fine-tuning offerings.

items.name: Voxtral
items.detail: Mistral's speech model family, including a TTS variant benchmarked by evaluators against ElevenLabs.

items.name: Grok (xAI)
items.detail: xAI's model family, current flagship Grok 4.6 (August 2026) tuned for coding/agentic work, with prior 4.5/4.3/4.1 variants and 'SuperGrok' consumer tiers.

items.name: Llama 4
items.detail: Meta's open-weight multimodal MoE model family (Scout, Maverick released April 2025; Behemoth indefinitely delayed), the most widely deployed open-weight ecosystem as of 2026.

items.name: Meta Superintelligence Labs / Muse
items.detail: Meta's restructured frontier-AI org under Alexandr Wang, which shipped the closed proprietary model Muse Spark (April 2026) that now powers some Meta AI features alongside Llama.

items.name: DeepSeek V4 (and R-series)
items.detail: DeepSeek's flagship Chinese open-weight MoE model, merging general and reasoning lineages, ~1M context, noted for very low token cost; successor to the market-moving R1.

items.name: Qwen
items.detail: Alibaba's open-weight model family (Qwen 3.6 series and prior), the most widely downloaded open-weight family on Hugging Face; Alibaba keeps its top 'Max' tier closed.

items.name: Kimi (Moonshot AI)
items.detail: Moonshot AI's open-weight Chinese model line (Kimi K3 cited in 2026), part of the competitive Chinese open-source frontier alongside DeepSeek and Qwen.

items.name: GLM (Zhipu / Z.ai)
items.detail: Zhipu AI's (rebranded Z.ai) open-weight model family (GLM-5.2 cited in 2026), another major Chinese open-source contender.

items.name: Amazon Bedrock
items.detail: AWS's managed multi-provider model API/platform (Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and others; 130+ model variants across 19 providers by 2026), with AgentCore for agent building.

items.name: Amazon Trainium
items.detail: AWS's custom AI training/inference chip line (Trainium2 in production, Trn3 UltraServer shipped Dec 2025, Trainium4 slated late 2026/2027), AWS's answer to Nvidia dependency.

items.name: Alexa+
items.detail: Amazon's generative-AI-rewritten voice assistant, built on Bedrock-hosted LLMs, notable for its agentic task orchestration across third-party services.

items.name: Microsoft Copilot / Microsoft Foundry
items.detail: Microsoft's enterprise AI stack: Copilot as the user-facing assistant across Microsoft 365/Windows, and Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) as the model-catalog and agent-building platform used by 80%+ of the Fortune 500.

items.name: GitHub Copilot
items.detail: Microsoft/GitHub's IDE-embedded AI coding assistant, cited with roughly 42% market share among AI coding tools in 2026.

items.name: Google TPU (Ironwood)
items.detail: Google's seventh-generation custom AI accelerator, positioned for large-scale inference, following the Trillium generation; central to the Google Cloud/Nvidia 'superstack' narrative.

items.name: AWS Trainium (Trn3/Trn4)
items.detail: See Amazon Trainium above; listed separately in hardware coverage as the AWS silicon line specifically competing with Nvidia GPUs for training/inference cost.

items.name: AMD Instinct MI-series
items.detail: AMD's data-center AI GPU line (MI300X-class and successors), AMD's primary challenger to Nvidia's Blackwell/Rubin GPUs; AMD also partnered with Cerebras in 2026 on disaggregated inference.

items.name: Cerebras (Wafer-Scale Engine)
items.detail: Cerebras's wafer-scale AI chip and inference cloud, IPO'd on Nasdaq May 2026 (~$56B valuation); competes with Groq on raw inference throughput.

items.name: Groq (LPU)
items.detail: Groq's Language Processing Unit inference chip and cloud service; Nvidia licensed Groq's technology and core team in a ~$20B deal announced December 2025, reshaping Groq into a cloud-software-focused entity.

items.name: Cursor
items.detail: Anysphere's AI-native code editor (VS Code fork), a benchmark product among professional developers for multi-file agentic refactors via its 'Composer' interface.

items.name: Windsurf / Devin (Cognition)
items.detail: Cognition's agentic coding product line: Windsurf (acquired by Cognition after a turbulent 2025) was rebranded 'Devin Desktop' in June 2026, alongside Cognition's autonomous-engineer agent Devin.

items.name: Perplexity
items.detail: Perplexity AI's answer-engine/search product, also known for its open-sourced R1 1776 model (a de-censored post-train of DeepSeek-R1).

items.name: Hugging Face
items.detail: The dominant open-model hosting hub and library ecosystem (Transformers, Hub); the reference point for open-weight model download/adoption metrics cited across the industry.

items.name: LangChain
items.detail: The widely used open-source framework/ecosystem (LangChain, LangGraph) for building LLM applications and agent orchestration, referenced across integration and tooling coverage.

items.name: vLLM
items.detail: The dominant open-source high-throughput LLM inference/serving engine, a standard reference point for self-hosted deployment performance.

items.name: Salesforce Agentforce
items.detail: Salesforce's agentic-AI platform layered on CRM/Data Cloud/MuleSoft; Agentforce ARR reported at $1.2B (up 205% YoY) in 2026, Salesforce's flagship counter to Microsoft's copilot approach.

items.name: Palantir AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform)
items.detail: Palantir's enterprise/government AI ops platform emphasizing governed, auditable agent actions; central to Palantir's US commercial growth narrative in 2026.

items.name: Midjourney
items.detail: The leading independent AI image-generation product, still regarded as best-in-class for artistic/photorealistic image quality; reported ~$500M revenue with a very small team.

items.name: Runway (Gen / GWM)
items.detail: Runway's AI video generation product line (Gen-3 and successors, GWM-1), cited as the leader in physics-accurate video for film/VFX use; ~$5.3B valuation in 2026.

items.name: Kling
items.detail: Kuaishou's AI video generation model (Kling, v3.0 cited), a leading motion-heavy-content competitor to Runway and Veo, prominent in Chinese and global video-gen coverage.

items.name: ElevenLabs
items.detail: The leading AI voice/speech company (TTS, voice cloning, Eleven v3), reported at an $11B valuation in 2026; a standard reference point for synthetic-voice quality.

items.name: Suno
items.detail: AI music-generation product, reported ~$300M ARR (404% growth) in 2026, alongside competitor Udio, in the fast-growing AI music segment.

items.name: Figure (Figure AI / Figure 03)
items.detail: Humanoid-robotics company whose robots (Figure 02/03) have a confirmed BMW production pilot and 10,000+ deployments across partner warehouses; valued ~$39B after an OpenAI-led round.

items.name: Tesla Optimus
items.detail: Tesla's humanoid robot program, deployed internally in Tesla factories with a stated goal of 10,000+ internal units by end of 2026 ahead of third-party sales.

items.name: 1X NEO
items.detail: 1X Technologies' consumer-oriented humanoid robot (NEO), targeting home use at roughly $20,000, distinct from the industrial focus of Figure and Optimus.

items.name: SWE-bench (Verified)
items.detail: The standard software-engineering coding benchmark (and its human-validated 'Verified' 500-task subset) used industry-wide to compare frontier and coding-agent model capability.

items.name: METR
items.detail: AI-evaluation nonprofit that benchmarks frontier model autonomous-task capability (HCAST, RE-Bench, SWAA) and publishes influential capability-trend analyses (e.g. task-horizon-doubling research).

items.name: Epoch AI
items.detail: Independent research org tracking AI compute trends and maintaining a cross-model benchmark database, a widely cited neutral data source for capability and compute trajectories.

input.summary: The "products" facet in AI-industry press coverage spans five overlapping clusters. First, frontier foundation-model families from the labs (Claude, GPT-5.x, Gemini 3, Grok, Mistral Large, Llama 4) plus the fast-moving Chinese open-weight tier (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM), each iterated frequently enough that version numbers themselves become news. Second, the compute-hardware layer that press treats as a product race in its own right: Nvidia's Blackwell-to-Rubin GPU transition plus its CUDA/NIM/DGX/Omniverse software stack, and the hyperscaler-custom-silicon response (Google TPU/Ironwood, AWS Trainium, AMD Instinct, plus specialist inference chipmakers Cerebras and Groq). Third, the applied-product layer built on those models: agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf/Devin, Codex), enterprise agent platforms (Microsoft Foundry/Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce, Palantir AIP, Amazon Bedrock/Alexa+), and generative media tools (Sora, Veo, Midjourney, Runway, Kling, ElevenLabs, Suno). Fourth, physical/embodied AI, dominated by humanoid-robot programs (Figure, Tesla Optimus, 1X) now treated as a distinct beat. Fifth, the infrastructure/measurement substrate the press relies on to make capability claims legible: open-model hubs and frameworks (Hugging Face, LangChain, vLLM), evaluation benchmarks (SWE-bench), and independent evaluators (METR, Epoch AI) alongside megaproject infrastructure like OpenAI's Stargate. Naming is volatile -- version suffixes (4.6, V4, 3.5 Flash) and rebrands (Windsurf→Devin Desktop, Azure AI Foundry→Microsoft Foundry) shift within months, so any pipeline should track family names as the stable anchor and treat specific version strings as time-stamped attributes.

structured_output.summary: The "products" facet in AI-industry press coverage spans five overlapping clusters. First, frontier foundation-model families from the labs (Claude, GPT-5.x/ChatGPT, Gemini 3, Grok, Mistral Large, Llama 4) plus the fast-moving Chinese open-weight tier (DeepSeek, Qwen, and their peers Kimi and GLM), each iterated frequently enough that version numbers themselves become news. Second, the compute-hardware layer that press treats as a product race in its own right: Nvidia's Blackwell-to-Rubin GPU transition plus its CUDA/NIM software stack, and the hyperscaler-custom-silicon response (Google TPU/Ironwood, AWS Trainium, AMD Instinct, plus specialist inference chipmakers Cerebras and Groq). Third, the applied-product layer built on those models: agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex), enterprise agent platforms (Microsoft Foundry/Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce, Palantir AIP, Amazon Bedrock/Alexa+), and generative media tools (Sora, Veo, Midjourney, Runway, ElevenLabs, Suno). Fourth, physical/embodied AI, dominated by humanoid-robot programs (Figure, Tesla Optimus, 1X) now treated as a distinct beat. Fifth, the infrastructure/measurement substrate the press relies on to make capability claims legible: open-model hubs and serving frameworks (Hugging Face, vLLM), evaluation benchmarks (SWE-bench), independent evaluators (METR, Epoch AI), and megaproject infrastructure like OpenAI's Stargate. Naming is volatile -- version suffixes (4.6, V4, 3.5 Flash) and rebrands (Windsurf→Devin Desktop, Azure AI Foundry→Microsoft Foundry) shift within months, so a pipeline should track family names as the stable anchor and treat specific version strings as time-stamped attributes.
